item.title: 40 years and counting for Chris “Naka” Nakamura
item.description: LIHUE — Feb. 18 was proclaimed Naka Day, and the Department of Water hosted a company breakfast to celebrate Chris “Naka” Nakamura’s job tenure with the DOW.

item.title: Trump touts economic record in State of the Union
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. President Donald Trump touted his economic record during the longest State of the Union address in history on Tuesday, boasting that he had ushered in a “golden age” as he sought to project an aura of success at a fraught moment for his presidency.

item.title: Mayor welcomes state champions
item.description: LIHUE — Kapaa High School boys soccer had the distinction of being the sole Kauai Interscholastic Federation squad to bring home the gold hardware in the seven winter sports offered by the Hawaii High School Athletic Association.

item.title: Hawaii congressional delegation pans Trump’s speech
item.description: Hawaii’s Democratic congressional delegation panned President Donald Trump’s State of the Union speech to Congress soon after it was over Tuesday night.

item.title: EDITORIAL: Cut hiking risks or incur rescue costs
item.description: Another year, another legislative bill seeking the reimbursement of search-and-rescue costs for trespassing hikers who require expensive extraction after they get stuck or suffer a medical emergency. It has become a perennial issue, and one that needs resolution for the sake of taxpayers’ wallets, the welfare of residents and visitors, and the safety of emergency responders.

item.title: Clean government groups push for special prosecutor
item.description: Advocates for campaign finance and other “clean government” reforms on Monday renewed the call for the appointment of a special prosecutor to conduct an independent probe of allegations that an unidentified “influential state legislator” accepted $35,000 in a paper bag.

item.title: Group created to protect Kauai from CRB
item.description: LIHUE — CRB Action Kauai, a new community-driven initiative, has formed to support Kauai residents, landowners, farmers, businesses and community groups responding to the growing threat of the Coconut Rhinoceros Beetle (CRB), an invasive pest impacting coconut and other palms across the island.

item.title: Hawaii lawmakers look to space for economic diversification
item.description: State leaders are considering what could be a leap toward a decades-old goal of making the aerospace industry a big part of Hawaii’s economy.

item.title: The 2026 Ka Pewa Youth Summit coming to Kauai
item.description: LIHUE — The 2026 Ka Pewa Youth Summit: Kupu Kelakela will take place on April 28 at the Kauai War Memorial Convention Hall. The second of its type in the state, it will be planned and executed in collaboration with student interns from Kauai and Maui.
